author: J. W. Taylor (Chicago)

Prairie library image a16-aic-taylor-fort-dearborn-monument-1893; the image store's copy is committed at data/sources/assets/fort_dearborn_monument_t3568/taylor_1893_three_quarter.jpg.
locator: The whole print: the monument from the south-west, a little west of square-on to its lettered front, so that the west faces of the base, plinth and die show narrowly at the left; the five figures in full detail against the sky; behind, the Pullman estate's ashlar 18th Street wall with a coped pier and a young street tree at right. The camera (data/reference_views/fort_dearborn_massacre_monument_1893/aic_taylor_1893.json) says how far it can be measured.
rights_note: A commercial photograph of the 1890s, public domain by age: the owner's ruling of 2026-10-27 on T-3161 (answer a) for J. W. Taylor's 1890s prints, applied here as it was to his 1729 Prairie print (aic_taylor_1445_pullman_from_sw) and his 1801 Kimball print. The Art Institute asks to be contacted for publication. Read for forms, places, depths and proportions; no texture or mesh is derived from it.

note: The only picture used here that sees a side of the pedestal. Through its camera the side faces read 85 px (base), 77 (plinth) and 61 (die) against fronts of 857, 596 and 546 px: base 2.85 m, plinth 1.8 m and die 1.6 m deep. The die's west face carries a narrow bronze panel. The group, left to right as the street sees it: the warrior striding left with the tomahawk raised in his right hand and a feather in his hair; Margaret Helm between the two men, her right arm reaching across to the warrior, her skirt to the rock; Black Partridge behind her, his left arm raised with the palm open against the blow, the musket slanting down past his right side; the surgeon on his back across the rock under them; the child at the right front, kneeling with both arms out. Monochrome (a toned print).
what_it_supplies: the five figures seen from the south-west, in full detail
what_it_does_not_supply: the group's rear and east side
